exposure: Maternal characteristics (e.g., city size of residence, parity, age at first child, employment status, diet, smoking status, education level)
outcome: Women and delivery characteristics (by planned birth setting)
Maternal hospitalization within the first week of delivery
Neonatal hospitalization within the first week of delivery
cohort: The study enrolled 1099 healthy low-risk women who delivered out-of-hospital with single, vertex babies between 37-42 weeks of gestation, alongside a 1:5 matched sample of comparable planned in-hospital deliveries.
finding: The study identified various maternal characteristics, such as living in larger cities and having higher education, as significant factors influencing the choice of out-of-hospital birth, which was associated with low rates of maternal (0.55%) and neonatal (1.73%) hospitalization within the first week for low-risk pregnancies.
mod_finding: The study found that certain maternal demographic and lifestyle factors were associated with choosing specific birth settings (home vs. freestanding midwifery unit; out-of-hospital vs. in-hospital), and reported low rates of adverse early outcomes for both mothers and neonates across these planned birth settings.
